title: Structs and Ownership
story: A struct is a box — when you move the box, everything inside moves with it. Structs own their fields, and moving a struct moves all its contents.
why: Understanding struct ownership is critical because structs are the building blocks of XIOM programs — ownership rules apply recursively to all fields.
analogy: A struct is like a shipping container — you can open it to look inside (&), rearrange contents (&mut), or move the entire container to a new owner.
try_it: Define a struct with a Vec field. Move the struct to a function and try using it afterward. Observe how the Vec moves with the struct.
tips: Moving a struct moves ALL its fields — you can't use any of them after
You can borrow individual fields through a struct borrow (&struct.field)
Partial moves are possible — you can move out one field while keeping the others
Think of struct ownership as recursive — each field follows the same rules
common_mistakes: Assuming fields are independent after a struct move — they all moved together
Trying to use a struct field after partially moving it — that field is gone
Forgetting that &struct.field borrows the entire struct, not just the field
